title: Finite polynomial inverse certificates descend along tensor base change to a stage
statement: Let $I$ be a directed preorder, $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ a diagram of commutative rings with colimit $A$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], $i_0\in I$, and $B_0$ a commutative $A_{i_0}$-algebra. Fix $n,m\geq0$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in B_0[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Regard $A$ and each $A_i$ for $i\geq i_0$ as $A_{i_0}$-algebras via their coprojection and transition. Let $f_{j,A}$ and $f_{j,i}$ be the coefficient images under $b\mapsto1\otimes b$ into $(A\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0)[x]$ and $(A_i\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0)[x]$. If $f_{j,A}$ admit a polynomial inverse certificate [def-weil-pbc-etale-polynomial-certificate], then $f_{j,i}$ admit one at some $i\geq i_0$. No finite-presentation hypothesis on $B_0$ is required.

proof.text: For the finite relation family f, its ideal square is generated by all products f_a f_b: Ideal.span_mul_span' and pow_two give this, identifying the generating set with the range on Fin m × Fin m. Ideal.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun expresses each certificate membership as a finite sum. Choose all coefficient families e and h. Subtracting these sums converts the memberships into equations equal to zero (private certificate_iff_equations).

Use the finite variable set (Fin m × Fin n) ⊕ ((Fin n × Fin n × Fin m) ⊕ (Fin m × (Fin m × Fin m))) for c,e,h, and equation set (Fin n × Fin n) ⊕ Fin m. Form q with constants f_j and their partial derivatives, variables c,e,h, multiplication, subtraction and finite sums. Evaluation recovers exactly the expanded two certificate identities. Coefficientwise partial differentiation commutes with map (MvPolynomial.pderiv_map). Apply finite polynomial equation descent to this explicitly constructed system.

At the resulting stage read c,e,h from their respective tuple components. Evaluation of the two types of equations gives the required expanded identities. The reverse implication of certificate_iff_equations reconstructs the two ideal memberships and hence the certificate. The finite-index constructions handle n=0 and m=0 unchanged.

lean.statement: theorem exists_stage_etalePolynomialCertificate {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [HasColimit F] (i₀ : I) (B₀ : Type v) [CommRing B₀] [Algebra (F.obj i₀) B₀] (n m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin n) B₀) : letI : Algebra (F.obj i₀) (colimit F : CommRingCat.{u}) := (colimit.ι F i₀).hom.toAlgebra EtalePolynomialCertificate (fun j ↦ MvPolynomial.map (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom : B₀ →+* (colimit F : CommRingCat.{u}) ⊗[F.obj i₀] B₀) (f j)) → ∃ (i : I) (hi : i₀ ≤ i), letI : Algebra (F.obj i₀) (F.obj i) := (F.map (homOfLE hi)).hom.toAlgebra EtalePolynomialCertificate (fun j ↦ MvPolynomial.map (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom : B₀ →+* F.obj i ⊗[F.obj i₀] B₀) (f j))
